To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of CYP450 variant alleles with interacting drugs and herbals, in a population with a history of psychosocial distress, can lead to akathisia and serotonin toxicity, with a potential to cause violence.
the incidence and severity of antidepressant-induced akathisias are associated with diminishing mutations of the genes that code for the CYP450 enzymes.

(i) variant alleles in Cyp450 genes are common in subjects with akathisia; (ii) these variant alleles are more common in akathisia than in random primary care subjects; (iii) the variant alleles in Cyps are more common in subjects with serotonin toxicity than in subjects with akinesia or parkinsonism; and (iv) the variant alleles are more prevalent in subjects who have been exposed to interacting drugs, herb or illicit substances
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of toxicity in the CYP450 pathway and its relation to the adverse effects of antidepressants.
the role of genetic and environmental factors in the development of akathisia, a serious side effect of many psychiatric drugs.
the role of CYP450 genes in the development of akathisia, a condition that can lead to violence and homicide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of antidepressants for psychopathology is a serious public health problem.
the use of antidepressant medications for psychosocial stress is a medical error that is associated with a high incidence of serious and sometimes fatal toxicity.
antidepressant-induced akathisias and related homicides are associated with diminishing mutations of the CYP2D6 and CYP2B19 genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CYP450 genes are the key to understanding the toxicity of psychotropic medications.
the use of antidepressants for psychopathology is not a safe and effective treatment.
the genetic profile of a patient, the drug prescribed and the co-prescribed medications and substances are key determinants in the risk of developing akathisia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no such thing as a safe antidepressant.
there is a strong need for better education of the general population, medical professionals, and regulatory agencies concerning the potential dangers of psychotropic drugs.
the use of antidepressants for the treatment of psychosocial distress is a major public health hazard.
